## Files you MAY edit
crates/callisto-graph/src/changed.rs (add functions and tests); crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs only if a re-export is needed; docs/architecture/versioning.md (one bullet). Nothing else.

## Read first
crates/callisto-graph/src/changed.rs: `changed_since_last_tag` already compares directory TREE IDS per package against its last tag (reverted edits do not count, cost does not grow with commit count). It answers "did anything change", which also counts tests, snapshots and docs. Measured on this repo (0.17.0 to 0.18.0): all crates had real src changes, so the real false positives would be test-only, snapshot-only and markdown-only edits. Also read crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs (`TagIndex::last_tag`), groups.rs (fixed/linked groups), aggregate.rs (how pending changesets name packages) and how `plan_version`/VersionPlan record which packages have a pending changeset.

## The work
1. `pub fn changed_source_files_since_last_tag(packages: &[&Package], tags: &TagIndex, git: &GitAccess<'_>, ignore: &[&str]) -> Result<BTreeMap<PackageId, Vec<PathBuf>>, GraphError>`: for each tagged package, the files under its directories that differ between its last tag and HEAD, excluding `ignore` pathspecs. Default ignore list exposed as `pub const DEFAULT_IGNORED_PATHS: &[&str]` covering `tests/`, `benches/`, `examples/`, `*.snap`, `*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Use git pathspec excludes (`:(exclude)` / `:!`) in as FEW git invocations as practical (batch per package, not per file). An untagged package yields all its tracked files. Uncommitted tracked changes count, like `changed_since_last_tag` does.
2. `pub fn uncovered_changes(changed: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Vec<PathBuf>>, covered: &BTreeSet<PackageId>, groups: ...) -> Vec<PackageId>`: packages with at least one changed file that are not covered. A package is covered if a pending changeset names it, OR it belongs to a FIXED or LINKED group where any member is covered (the group moves together). Look at how groups are represented in groups.rs and pick the least invasive signature; keep it pure (no git, no IO) so it is trivially testable.
3. Tests with git fixtures (see crates/callisto-fixtures and existing tests in changed.rs): a src edit is reported; a tests/-only, snapshot-only, markdown-only edit is NOT; a revert (edit then undo) is not; an untagged package; two packages where only one changed; a fixed group where one member has a changeset covers the sibling; a linked group likewise; a package outside any group with no changeset is reported; ignore list override. Plus a proptest on `uncovered_changes` (proptest is already a dev-dependency): result is a subset of changed packages and never contains a covered package or a package whose group-mate is covered.
4. Mutation check: break the exclude pathspec and the group-coverage rule one at a time, confirm a test fails each time, restore.
5. One bullet in docs/architecture/versioning.md describing the two functions and that they are not wired anywhere yet.

## Summary

The release PR body now says where merging will publish each package, and leads with a caution when the release would fail.

- `compose-pr-body --preview <file> --publish-plan`, run after `version`, plans the release of the versioned working tree with `plan_workspace_release` in preview mode: offline, no registry lookup, nothing published. The body gets a "Merging will publish" table listing each package's registries, git tag, GitHub release and assets.
- A plan that the release itself would refuse becomes a stop finding, and the body opens with a `[!CAUTION]` naming the error in place of the compatibility note. Because it is the same planning step the release runs, the body cannot name a target the release would not publish.
- The release PR action passes `--publish-plan`. The spec (REL-PR-10), the architecture doc and the action contract test are updated.

Registry-side checks that need the network (a name another project owns, crates.io metadata) are not part of the preview plan, so the caution covers only the offline refusals.

- `cargo test -p callisto-graph -p callisto-cli` pass, including a test that plans a real versioned fixture to crates.io plus a tag, and rendering tests for planned, blocked and absent outlooks.
- Mutation check: disabling the caution makes its test fail.
- `cargo clippy` and `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`, the release PR action contract test, and the two release workflow contract scripts pass.

Not run: CI, and the action end to end on GitHub.

- [Current Work Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md (local only, never PR it), rewritten 2026-10-23 (stale; refresh pending); older plans in .claude/plans/archive/; verify an item against code before treating it as open.
- [Nov 2026 Cleanup Trail](project_cleanup_trail_2026_11.md) — verified findings, open PRs, not-bugs and pending owner decisions; analysis and release-pr-apply design live in .claude/plans/ (local only).
- [No Stacks For Now](feedback_no_stacks_for_now.md) — Independent PRs off main, one at a time; a four-deep stack caused merge-up commits, a re-sign force-push and conflicts (supersedes Use gh stack).
- [Always Sign Commits](feedback_sign_commits.md) — I committed with gpgsign=false and unsigned commits blocked merging; never override signing, spot-check `verification.reason` is `valid` after pushing.
- [PR Body Emoji Is Intentional](feedback_pr_body_emoji_intentional.md) — the few emoji in the release PR body are settled product output; never flag them against the AGENTS.md rule.
- [No Over-Engineering, Confirm Intent](feedback_no_overengineering_confirm_intent.md) — guard script for a loud cheap failure was rejected; Callisto features go in Rust not shell; confirm stated config choices and check PR state before pushing.
- [Prove With the Real Tool](feedback_prove_with_the_real_tool.md) — Fake-tool tests and clean compiles hid the 0.10.1 gh credential regression; reproduce auth/release/registry paths with the real tool, test the failing case first, state what is unproven.
- [Callisto Self-Release Incident — Durable Memory](project_release_self_hosting_incident_2026-09.md) — Claude invented and later misattributed the release approval gate, misunderstood rerun semantics, and repeatedly declared fixes before publication; records non-negotiable policy, verified failures, corrective architecture, and required incident protocol.
- [Hardcoded Values — Proactive Search Required](feedback_hardcoded_values.md) — User repeatedly frustrated by missed hardcoded values; always include a dedicated pass in any audit or fix session.
- [Track 0: gix WASI spike — NO-GO verdict](project_track0_wasi_verdict.md) — mmap ENOSYS in WASI blocks all gix object reads; callisto-moon exec-seam must use warpgate_pdk::exec_command.
- [Publish Pipeline Audit — 38 bugs, fix ordering, semantic coupling map](project_publish_pipeline_audit.md) — Full adversarial audit complete; 5 P0s, 11 P1s, 15+ P2s; three root patterns; phased fix sequence with dependency order.
- [Parallel Fixing Anti-Pattern](feedback_parallel_fixing.md) — Parallel agents for fixes fail on semantically coupled systems even across different files; use parallel for investigation only.
- [Validate Each Fix Individually](feedback_validate_each_fix.md) — Run targeted tests after every individual fix; do not batch changes and rely solely on final CI run.
- Architecture: ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/architecture/ (moved from .claude/semantic-model on 2026-09-25) — read before implementation work.
- [Canon Pipeline Scope](feedback_canon_pipeline_scope.md) — Skip canon ceremony for targeted bug fixes with RED tests already written; canon auditor loops infinitely on implementation-detail prose.
- [Workspace Audit 2026-08](project_workspace_audit_2026-08.md) — CLOSED: 8-dimension audit, all critical/high + all 31 medium/low findings re-verified fixed as of 2026-08-27.
- [Found Code Needs Same Rigor](feedback_found_code_needs_same_rigor.md) — Committing pre-existing uncommitted code after only "compiles + existing tests pass" missed a zero-test-coverage regression; found/inherited code needs the same TDD/adversarial rigor as freshly-written code.
- [Manifest Persist Track](project_manifest_persist_track.md) — Both Spec A (mutate/persist split) and Spec B (write-batching) shipped; the apply_version_plan redundant-open/persist audit finding is fully closed.
- [Reviewer Must Actually Run Checks](feedback_reviewer_must_actually_run_checks.md) — lambda-reviewer falsely reported clippy clean once; always instruct review agents to run commands for real, not infer results.
- [Iterate Reviews in Foreground](feedback_iterate_reviews_in_foreground.md) — Background agent notifications were unreliable across a multi-round spec/plan review loop; user called it out twice — run tight revise-review cycles in the foreground.
- [PR #5 Release Pipeline Hardening](project_pr5_release_pipeline_hardening.md) — Fixed-group max-severity-wins config + no-compounding test, plus SPEC-005 ReleaseEntry.is_prerelease shipped end to end; all CI green.
- [Track 7: Revwalk Bounding + Git Fixture Hermeticity Gap](project_git_fixture_hermeticity_gap.md) — nextest+global gpgsign causes ~120s hangs across ~13 test files; deferred as its own future track.
- [Diagnose, Don't Guess, Environment Issues](feedback_diagnose_dont_guess_environment_issues.md) — User rejected an unverified guess (XProtect); always confirm root cause with a falsifiable test before reporting it.
- [Recover Stale Agent Results After Session Interruption](feedback_recover_stale_agent_results.md) — Read the raw .output JSONL transcript directly when ListAgents/TaskOutput shows "completed" but the result looks like a stale mid-flight placeholder, instead of re-dispatching duplicates.
- [Always Use Plugins](feedback_always_use_plugins.md) — Route PR/commit narration and audits through courier/ranger/etc. plugin agents by default, not freehand, even when I already have full context.
- [Terse Comments Only](feedback_terse_comments.md) — One short line max, only for non-obvious WHY; stop writing multi-line prose comments in code/config even though CLAUDE.md already says this.
- [Cargo Slowness Root Cause](project_cargo_slowness_target_pollution.md) — Hours-long builds were a polluted target/debug (1.7M .o files); wipe it, split-debuginfo=off, one invocation shape, no parallel builds; cold build is 31 s.
- [No Red-Green, Lean Tokens](feedback_no_red_green_lean_tokens.md) — User dropped red-green testing and wants lean token spend; no heavy agent gating loops; CLI product tag callisto@{version} is intentional.
- [Never Hard-Wrap Prose](feedback_never_hard_wrap_prose.md) — PR descriptions and all Markdown: one line per paragraph, never manual line breaks.
- [Succinct Written Artifacts](feedback_succinct_written_artifacts.md) — Changesets, PR bodies, docs: short, plain, no AI slop or backstory.
- [No Session Links](feedback_no_session_links.md) — Never put claude.ai session URLs/Claude-Session trailers in commits or PRs; public repo, private sessions.
- [Verify Before Recommending](feedback_verify_before_recommending.md) — Check code, callers and sibling repos before presenting any recommendation; audit findings are leads, not conclusions.
- [No Thin ADRs](feedback_no_thin_adrs.md) — ADRs only for significant decisions, with rejected options, enforcement and revisit triggers; process rules aren't ADRs.
- [Budget: Lean Pipeline](feedback_budget_lean_pipeline.md) — weekly token budget; leanest pipeline that still catches bugs; no cleanup agents or rework the user has to review.
- [Use gh stack](feedback_use_gh_stack.md) — stacked PRs must be native GitHub stacks (gh stack link); plain chained PRs get no CI.
- [Agent Context Briefs](feedback_agent_context_briefs.md) — curated 2-4k token briefs, one agent per PR via SendMessage, small fixes directly; no forks of long sessions.
- [Local Tracking, Not PRs](feedback_local_tracking_not_prs.md) — Tracking/handoff plans live in .claude/plans/ (git-excluded); never commit or PR them (PR #201 was closed for this).
- [Worktree Guard Command Shapes](feedback_worktree_guard_commands.md) — worktree-isolated sessions refuse heredocs, compound commands and text naming git; use /usr/bin/git and scripts written with the Write tool.
- [Check PR Overlap Before Parallel Branches](feedback_check_pr_overlap_before_parallel_branches.md) — run a pairwise merge-tree check on a PR batch, stack the overlapping ones, hold repo-wide refactors, give a merge order.
- [Measure Value Before Building](feedback_measure_value_before_building.md) — tag hints reverted (#342): gain was noise-level; measure A/B (process counts + wall) and agree it earns its code before opening PRs.
- [Trails: Feature First, Link Before the PR](feedback_trails_feature_first.md) — group by outcome, description = the work, create the trail and link branches before gh pr create; auto-trails cannot be reparented via CLI.
- [Entire Auto-Push Is Intended](feedback_entire_auto_push_intended.md) — owner wants Entire session/checkpoint pushes to the public origin; never flag or disable it.

content.text: The remote deletion was denied by the classifier as a destructive git action, so those three are yours to run. Recording a worktree-naming rule so this doesn't recur, then the summary.

input.content:
---
name: feedback-worktree-hygiene
description: Name worktrees for the task, one task per worktree; flag a stale worktree name instead of silently reusing it
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A long session kept working in `.claude/worktrees/macos-15-runners` (named for its first task) for weeks of unrelated PRs, and the user objected: "Why are we in a macos 15 worktree???? wtf".

**Why:** The folder name is what the user sees in `git worktree list` and PR tooling; a stale name makes the work look like it belongs to a finished task, and merged branches and agent worktrees pile up.

**How to apply:** Start a task in a worktree named for it. When a session outlives its first task, say so and switch to a freshly named worktree (create it with `/usr/bin/git worktree add`, then enter it) before cutting the next branch. Delete merged local branches after each PR lands (`git branch -d`, which refuses unmerged work). Remote branch deletion is blocked by the auto-mode classifier, so hand the user the exact `git push origin --delete` line. Never remove another job's worktrees (`~/.claude/jobs/*/tmp/wt/*`) or an agent worktree holding uncommitted work. See [[feedback-no-stacks-for-now]].

lastPrompt: Change #78 has some review findings. Pleare review, verify, find patterns and address appropriately. Resolve or dismiss as required.

content.text:
I deleted 16 stale local branches and resolved the three #470 findings. The remote branch deletes and the worktree removals are left for you.

**Findings on #470 (change #78):** all three were real and are fixed in `d58b697cb`, then resolved.
- **Merged rows:** `cargo/shared` and `npm/shared` were collapsed into one row. Rows are now keyed by the qualified id.
- **Wrong package list:** an empty selection listed every unreleased package, not the ones the release will hold. The plan now selects exactly the bumped packages.
- **Not actually offline:** the preview planner could observe registries when `origin` was set, so my "offline" claim was wrong. There is now `plan_workspace_release_offline`.
- **Tests:** a unit test for the row keying, and an end-to-end test that records every program the offline plan starts and asserts only `git`. Re-enabling observation makes that test fail.
- **Checks run:** the full `callisto-graph` and `callisto-cli` suites, clippy, docs and the action contract all pass.

**Branches deleted locally:** 15 fully merged branches plus `feat/rebase-entry-headings`. The latter was one commit that `git cherry` shows already in `main` as the same patch (via #469). The merged ones were `chore/remove-dead-code`, `chore/remove-workspace-version-write`, `ci/drop-release-pr-notes`, `ci/release-gate-parallel`, `docs/align-with-code`, `docs/comments-present-tense`, `feat/emit-release-preview`, `feat/release-notes-model`, `feat/release-pr-headlines`, four `fix/*` branches and `refactor/markdown-module`.

**Left alone on purpose**
- `feat/pr-body-publish-plan` and `feat/uncovered-changes`: open PRs #470 and #471.
- `feat/changeset-markers`: it shows as "merged" only because the agent never committed. Its worktree holds the unreviewed markers work.
- `slopfix/*` and their worktrees: they belong to another job (`~/.claude/jobs/45cd44b5`).
- The `worktree-agent-*` branches and `agent-*` worktrees: needed until #471 merges and you decide on the markers work.

**For you to run** (the classifier blocked these as destructive; all three are fully merged into `main`):
```
git push origin --delete fix/config-and-error-conformance fix/duration-token-scrub-git-failure fix/status-strict-and-artifact-input-message
```
Once #470 merges and this session ends, remove the stale worktree and the stale `main` checkout:
```
git worktree remove .claude/worktrees/macos-15-runners
git -C /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto pull --ff-only
```
The `macos-15-runners` worktree is locked while I'm in it, so I can't remove it myself. I recorded a rule to name worktrees for their task and flag a stale name. For the next branch I'll use a freshly named worktree.
